chunks: Know that self-admiration is contrary to propriety (of action) and is a calamity for the mind. Therefore, increase your striving and do not become a treasurer for (wealth to be inherited by) others. When you have been guided on the right path humble yourself before Allāh as much as you can.

key_terms.الْإِعْجَابُ: Self-admiration or vanity, a spiritual defect
key_terms.الْخَازِنُ: Treasurer or keeper, implying one who stores wealth for others to inherit

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual danger of self-admiration according to Imam Ali's advice to Hasan?
ai.summary: In this instruction to his son Hasan following the Battle of Siffin, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies self-admiration (al-i'jab) as a spiritual defect that corrupts the intellect and leads one away from divine truth. He contrasts this with the virtue of diligent, independent effort (kadh) and prescribes profound humility (khashi'a) before God as the proper response to success, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing worldly action with spiritual modesty.
